items.stem: A maximal effort lasting about 8 seconds (e.g. a short sprint or single heavy lift) is fuelled predominantly by which energy system?

options.rationale: Correct: very short, maximal efforts rely mainly on the immediately available phosphagen system.
The oxidative system dominates during prolonged, lower-intensity activity.
Glycolysis contributes more as effort extends beyond ~10 seconds; it is not dominant for an 8-second maximal effort.
Protein is a minor fuel source and not dominant for short maximal efforts.

items.explanation: Correct: very short, maximal efforts rely mainly on the immediately available phosphagen system.

items.stem: When sequencing a single testing session, which ordering best protects data quality?

options.text: Non-fatiguing and power/agility tests before maximal strength and anaerobic-capacity tests
options.rationale: Correct: placing less fatiguing, higher-skill tests first prevents prior fatigue from biasing results.

options.text: Maximal strength testing first, then agility
options.rationale: Heavy maximal work first would fatigue and bias later power/agility tests.

options.text: Anaerobic capacity sprints first, then skill tests
options.rationale: Exhausting anaerobic tests first would compromise subsequent tests.
Inconsistent ordering reduces reliability of comparisons.

items.explanation: Correct: placing less fatiguing, higher-skill tests first prevents prior fatigue from biasing results.

items.stem: Select TWO principles that should guide resistance-training program design for a novice athlete.

options.rationale: Correct: gradual progressive overload drives adaptation while managing risk.

options.text: Building a base of technique and general strength before high-intensity plyometrics
options.rationale: Correct: a strength/technique base should precede intense plyometric work.
Frequent maximal testing is excessive and raises injury risk for novices.

options.text: Avoiding any rest between all sets
options.rationale: Appropriate rest is required for quality and safety.

options.text: Ignoring exercise technique to add load faster
options.rationale: Sacrificing technique for load increases injury risk.

items.explanation: Correct: gradual progressive overload drives adaptation while managing risk.
